neighbours.label: the writer checking that the reader follows (Make sense?, Does that make sense?, Are you with me?, Know what I mean?), as opposed to sentences of the same shape about something else, including the same words without the check (makes no sense to try, know what I mean to do)
fire: You pour it in slowly, then stir. Make sense?
So the tax goes up when prices fall. Does all that make sense?
Are you following me so far?
You add the two numbers first. Got it?
That's the whole trick. You see what I mean?
It's a hard habit to break. Know what I'm saying?
Still with me? Good, let's keep going.
I hope that cleared things up for you.
quiet: You pour it in slowly, then stir. Add salt.
So the tax goes up when prices fall. Does all that make money?
Are you following him so far?
You add the two numbers first. Got a pen?
That's the whole trick. You know what I mean to do.
It's a hard habit to break. It makes no sense to try.
Still with him? Good, let's keep going.
I hope that cleaned things up for you.

notes: Card: '?' x5, ' sense' x3, ' me' x2, ' Sound', ' sound', ' made', ' mean'.
